units.text: Apple had a big September, but it’s set to keep momentum going in October with several rumored product unveilings soon that we’ve waited a long time for.
#1: MacBook Pro / Ultra redesign with touchscreen
The Mac is a long-time touchscreen holdout, but that’s finally set to change with a new MacBook Pro (or MacBook Ultra) product expected to launch in October.

Apple’s next-gen MacBook Pro will introduce a brand new industrial design—the first such overhaul in five years. And in addition to touch support, it will boast an OLED display, Dynamic Island, and possibly a C2 cellular modem option.

It’s been a long time since the MacBook Pro got a new look. But far longer since touchscreens became the norm, and Apple decided to forego them on the Mac. I’m excited to see how touch might enhance the experience of the Mac moving forward.
#2: New Apple TV 4K
There’s never been a longer wait for new Apple TV hardware than the current drought of updates. Apple’s latest model, the third-gen Apple TV 4K, was introduced in 2022.
Rumors indicate we’ll finally get a new Apple TV 4K in October, headlined by a powerful A19 or A19 Pro chip and Siri AI support.

This summer Apple raised prices on most of its products, including the Apple TV. That means the four-year-old Apple TV 4K now costs $199—far more than the $129 price it launched at. Here’s hoping the new Apple TV doesn’t go any higher.
#3: ‘HomePad’

Rumors of a HomePod with a display have been around for nearly as long as the HomePod’s existence. But they ramped up in 2024 when Mark Gurman offered an in-depth report on what’s commonly called the ‘HomePad.’

HomePad is a smart display with built-in speaker that will reportedly spearhead Apple’s renewed push into home products. It will have a new OS that resembles parts of iOS, tvOS, and watchOS, including a StandBy-like mode.
Siri AI is expected to be central to the product, which will also feature a camera, customizable widgets, and built-in Apple apps like Photos, Notes, Music, Calendar, and more.
Which new Apple products in October and beyond are you most excited for? Let us know in the comments.

Currently, taking an Apple Watch screenshot simply causes the screen to flash, then the screenshot is added to your Photos library.

It’s unclear if Apple plans to implement this change in a forthcoming watchOS 27.2 beta, or if it needs more time for development. But if it doesn’t make the cut in watchOS 27.2, we’re still likely to see it come to the Apple Watch in the near future.

A few days ago, we covered the many features Apple added to its parental controls suite across its devices with the release of iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27.

As Apple explains, everything starts with setting up a child account, which enables parents to choose age-appropriate safeguards for their personal devices.

With that in place, Apple explains how parents can control which types of apps their kids can access, approve new apps and games through Ask to Buy, and use the new Ask to Browse feature to approve or deny access to websites in Safari.

units.text: What's Gone in macOS Golden Gate and What's Next in macOS 28

With macOS Golden Gate, Apple phased out several legacy features and services, cutting support for older devices and accessories. More cuts are coming in macOS 28 as Apple continues to root out lingering Intel features.
Here's everything that's been dropped.

Support for Intel Macs - ‌macOS Golden Gate‌ is the first version of macOS that runs only on Apple silicon Macs. Intel Macs can't run it and are limited to macOS Tahoe. Apple still plans to offer security updates through fall 2028.

Boot Camp Assistant - Since ‌macOS Golden Gate‌ doesn't run on Intel Macs, it doesn't support Boot Camp. Apple silicon Macs require virtualization software like Parallels or VMware Fusion to run Windows.

Rosetta 2 (Temporarily) - Upgrading to ‌macOS Golden Gate‌ removes Rosetta, but if you have an app installed that requires it, you can reinstall it. ‌macOS Golden Gate‌ is the last version of macOS that will have full Rosetta support.
Apple Filing Protocol - Apple deprecated AFP back in macOS Sequoia 15.5, and there is no AFP client at all in ‌macOS Golden Gate‌.

Time Capsule Backups - With no support for AFP, Time Capsule no longer works with Macs running ‌macOS Golden Gate‌. Time Capsule requires AFP or SMBv1, but Time Machine backups now use the SMBv2 or SMBv3 protocol.

AirPort Utility - AirPort Utility is no longer included when you install ‌macOS Golden Gate‌. If you had the app before updating, you can still use it, but Apple makes no guarantee that it still works. AirPort Utility lets users manage AirPort base stations like the AirPort Extreme and AirPort Express.

macOS 28, which is expected in fall 2027, will largely drop support for Rosetta 2. Most apps that rely on Rosetta will not open on Macs running macOS 28, though Apple is making an exception for some legacy games that are unmaintained.

In ‌macOS Golden Gate‌, you'll see a warning when using any app that relies on Rosetta, so you're aware that the app won't continue to work in the future without a developer update. You can also see which apps are affected by going to Settings > General > About > Intel-Based Apps and then clicking on Details.

一、结束对 Intel Mac 的支持
macOS Golden Gate 是首个仅可在 Apple 芯片 Mac 上运行的 macOS 版本。IT之家援引博文介绍，Intel Mac 无法运行此版本，最高只能停留在 macOS 26 Tahoe 系统。不过苹果承诺为其提供安全更新至 2028 年秋季。
二、Boot Camp 助理
Boot Camp 助理同步移除，意味着 M 系列 Mac 目前不能像 Intel Mac 那样通过 Boot Camp 安装成真正的原生双系统。
使用 Apple Silicon 芯片的 Mac 需要 Parallels 或 VMware Fusion 等虚拟化软件才能运行 Windows 11 系统。
三、Rosetta 2（暂时停用）
Rosetta 2 是苹果开发的指令集转译层，允许为 Intel Mac 编译的应用在 Apple Silicon Mac 上运行。用户无需修改应用即可使用旧软件，但性能略有损失，苹果正推动开发者原生适配 ARM 架构。
如果用户安装了需要 Rosetta 的应用，可以重新安装。不过 macOS 27 Golden Gate 是最后一个完全支持 Rosetta 的 macOS 版本。
在 macOS 27 Golden Gate 中，用户使用任何依赖 Rosetta 的应用时会出现警告提示。用户可通过“设置”>“通用”>“关于本机”>“基于 Intel 的应用”查看受影响应用列表。
macOS 28 预计 2027 年秋季发布，将基本停止 Rosetta 2 支持，多数依赖转译层的应用无法运行。
四、苹果文件协议（AFP）
AFP 是苹果开发的文件共享协议，用于 Mac 之间或 Mac 与服务器之间的文件传输。因安全性与兼容性问题，苹果已用 SMB 协议替代，Golden Gate 中彻底移除 AFP 客户端。
五、Time Capsule 备份
Time Capsule 是苹果已停产的无线路由器，内置硬盘支持 Time Machine 无线备份。因依赖 AFP 或 SMBv1 协议，在 macOS 27 Golden Gate 及后续系统中无法继续使用。Time Machine 备份现统一采用 SMBv2 或 SMBv3 协议。
六、AirPort 实用工具

‘Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars’ is back

Less than one year after the premiere of the first season of “Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars,” the show is back for a new eight-episode run telling the stories of restaurants around the world as they try to earn, keep, or add to their Michelin stars.

The show, which is hosted by food and travel expert Jesse Burgess and executive-produced by Gordon Ramsay and Studio Ramsay Global, chronicles restaurants, chefs, and their teams, as well as the relentless work that goes into earning and maintaining the culinary world’s highest recognition.
As Apple announced a few days ago, the new season features 16 restaurants across Europe, the US, and Brazil, each at a different point in their pursuit.
Following today’s two-episode premiere, new episodes will drop every Friday through November 6.
Here’s Apple TV on what to expect from the second season of “Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars”:

Across season two, “Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars” follows 16 restaurants at pivotal moments in their journeys: A chef and his family risk everything to put a tiny island on Michelin’s map. Two generations of a legendary culinary family pursue recognition on their own terms. Two chefs voluntarily give up their Star when they open a new restaurant and have just 52 days to win it back. One sandwich shop transforms into a fine dining restaurant each night, while a young couple seeks to put Filipino cuisine at the center of one of America’s most competitive dining scenes. Their circumstances could hardly be more different, yet each faces the same uncertainty: When Michelin makes its decision, will everything they have strived for be enough?
